scope: Conservative naming classification of the 251 previously inventoried files. Counts are files, not distinct oracle mechanisms. This is not a repository-wide registry or a new guide-conformance audit.

files.mechanism: Angular source/mount/current/cleanup adapter passes a LiveQueryDriver to runSuite in packages/db/tests/conformance/suite-oracle.ts. Additional checks are fixed publication examples or driver/scope calibration; this file does not compute independent product expectations.

One hardcoded PostgreSQL update history: initialRow and updatedRow are supplied literals, and expectExactRow merely wraps those literals into public/durable expected observations. The remaining tests check diagnostic helpers. There is no independent history reducer or generalized reference rule here.
Holds production sync begin/commit and hydration return, records applied-receipt reach and public/durable rows, and exposes a browser probe. It does not compute an independently expected result.

Single insert/hard-close/reopen regression with a literal row and manually enumerated phase/public/durable expectations. expectedPublicObservation only projects the supplied expected record; the PostgreSQL SELECT verifies the same literal, rather than supplying a differential reference computation. Additional cases test polling/diagnostic helpers.
Creates the Electric/persisted Collection, parks its durable adapter write, records real public/durable rows, and exposes insert/recovery controls. Expected-result judgments live in the spec.

Two named legacy-loss examples run the same fixed seed/add-row/handoff/reopen trace. expectedRows only sorts the explicitly supplied fixture rows; rowsAfter is a case-table expectation. No independent transition model or reusable query-result computation is exercised.

Creates real host Collections, edits durable storage to establish legacy-loss input, and transports actual Collection/resume observations. Poisoning checks confirm fixture setup, not an independent expected-result law.

One real-Web-Lock receiving witness with a fixed 15-second deadline and hardcoded TimeoutError, removed pending lock, and SELECT 1 expectations. Important host regression, but no independent generalized deadline/state oracle is invoked.
One fixed item ID and two-tab load, followed by one invalid-wire value. Expected row, route flags, counts, and error path are literal example assertions, without an independent reference computation.

Supplies a controlled QueryClient-backed provider, records local request fields and wire posts, starts a real filtered live query, and exposes its actual rows. Parsing the request in the provider supplies test data, not expected-result judgment.

The fixed native storm executes the independently defined K=1 fairness rule through its page companion and rejects any returned violation. This is a narrow receiving oracle, not merely the fixed row assertions: the shared checker derives permitted persist IDs/counts from the scenario and compares every hydrate checkpoint. Fixed native scenarios do not make that generalized independent rule a hardcoded trace. Borderline ownership is split across the page and spec, but the spec owns pass/fail at the semantic checkpoint.

Chooses two fixed host scenarios, runs the shared production driver with real OPFS, invokes the imported fairness checker, and transports its violation result. It defines neither the independent fairness rule nor test acceptance; the receiving spec rejects that result. Dedicated oracle support remains a fixture.

Although mostly example tests, it also contains genuine generalized independent routing and retention laws. Generated collection counts/registration permutations/target IDs drive real coordinator RPC; expected call counts are computed solely from target identity (index === targetIndex ? 1 : 0). A separate generated release-order ledger decrements independent remaining count and compares both retained maps after each action.

Computes the expected raw settlement ledger from delivery stage, request count, release direction, and completed prefix. For mixed histories, the independent index predicate determines fulfilled versus rejected outcomes before comparison with actual production opener/query settlements. Existing pre-PR oracle name remains untouched.

referenceMessage independently concatenates primary/cause fields from scalar input; generated error classes/messages invoke the production worker init handler and compare the complete response to that computation. Existing pre-PR name is untouched.

Contains explicit independent reusable models: remoteLeaseHistoryViolations computes expected loads/unloads/remaining acquisitions from the history, and PerCollectionRouteOracle maps owner plus Collection identity to expected adapter. Generated production histories compare their captured traces against those models. Existing pre-PR name is untouched.

For generated logical admission histories, independently derives expected hydrate rows and persist FIFO order and applies findSharedDriverFairnessViolation to actual shared-driver observations. Fixed/random campaigns execute this comparison; the wrong-scheduler control checks sensitivity. Existing pre-PR name is untouched.

Defines createFairnessReference: the expected bound is min(persistCount, 1 + hydrateIndex * K), with FIFO permitted persist IDs. findSharedDriverFairnessViolation compares real checkpoint identities/counts/remaining work to that rule. Also contains production-driver mechanics, but its independent reusable checker establishes definition ownership. Existing pre-PR name is untouched.
Creates a temporary SQLite database and platform harness, then registers the shared suite. No expected-result computation or product assertion is defined.
Only lifecycle hooks, harness lookup, and invocation of the shared conformance registration function. It imports judgment; it does not own it.
Literal persisted-conformance test-name manifest and name-formatting function support registration/native result collection. They neither run production nor judge a modeled result.

A fixed lexical witness inserts the five authored names A10, A2, Z, a, ä in a fixed permutation and compares real rows to that literal sequence. The local expectOrderedRows closure is exact equality against this example, not an independently computed collation rule; negative controls do not change its role.

Fixed concurrent-query examples assert sizes, nonemptiness, differing offsets, and equal result counts among identical queries. The 20-query burst compares every count to the first production count; it provides no independently computed deduplication/load model. This weak same-input peer comparison is borderline, so conservatively restore the example-suite name.

Independent userPostPairs and withComments loops compute left-join pairs/triples from captured fixture rows, including unmatched children. Real query projections are compared against those reference rows through createJoinOracle, with independent fixture ordering for ordered cases.

Captures every real subscribeChanges batch alongside callback-visible complete rows and executes expectNotificationHistory on that production history. The imported checker independently reconstructs row state from each insert/update/delete and checks every callback and final row set.

Maintains independent activeUsers/posts maps from authored commands. check computes expected visible posts by filtering modeled posts through modeled user activity, compares complete production entries, and also applies notification-history reconstruction to real callback observations.

Authored insertion/deletion/update histories compare observed peers plus a particular inserted row, and a fixed eleven-row ordered witness checks literal slices before/after one age change. Generic equality/capture helpers do not independently evaluate a query or maintain a generalized mutation model. The insert-then-delete frame check has a metamorphic flavor; conservatively restore the example-suite name.

createWindowOracle clones independent fixture rows, sorts with a test-side comparator, and computes ranked.slice(offset, offset + limit). It checks real query rows for exact cardinality, unique identities, unchanged values, and legal rank ties across window scenarios.

Computes expected rows by native fixture filtering (and independent ordering for orderedAliceRows), then captures real query values and compares their complete selected rows. The reference predicate evaluation is separate from the production query builder.

Fixed progressive-load smoke/regression cases check readiness, limits, literal predicates, and peer-query membership. The snapshot deduplication case runs three identical age=30 queries and compares them to the first result; there is no independent progressive/publication state model. Treat the limited peer comparison conservatively as an example.

Generic assertion utilities compare caller-supplied IDs/counts, apply a caller-supplied predicate, or check adjacent ordering. They do not derive complete product expectations or own a domain reference computation; the retained pagination/predicate suites own their reference fixture computations.

expectNotificationHistory independently reconstructs a Map from notification events, checks event admission/previous values, and requires each callback-visible row set and final rows to equal that reconstructed state. Named suites execute it against real production callbacks.

A bounded per-branch input ledger computes the expected invocation vector from the selected active branch and next branch, then compares every real D2 operator call count after each graph.run(). This is a small generalized work rule across branch positions; the separate reversed-registration case is a fixed example.

expectRetryHistory derives getter-read counts from the generated rejecting position, failed-attempt count, and untouched suffix. It checks the thrown error and all read counts after each real hash attempt, compares the successful result with a separately built structural copy, and checks subsequent cache reuse.

An independent reachable-indegree/Kahn model predicts cycle rejection. For acyclic generated graphs, the checker unfolds shared nodes into fresh trees and requires real hash agreement; for reachable cycles it requires repeated rejection.

A spec-level canonical identity encoding derives expected equality independently of the production hasher. Generated specs are realized into runtime values and checked in both comparison directions and through hash compatibility, including a second module with forced collisions and separately constructed cyclic pairs.

The checker computes reachable acyclicity with an indegree model over a separate graph specification. Realizations mix object, array, Map, Set, and symbol edge carriers; cyclic results must reject and acyclic shared graphs must hash like their independent unfoldings.

Generated metamorphic laws compare hash results for independently constructed clones and reordered object properties. The concrete judgment includes insertion-order independence, equal byte/date contents, and declared type-marker distinctions; it is not only deterministic-output examples.

captureHashSession reloads the production module while recording/replaying Math.random initialization draws and attaching environment metadata. HashReplayError preserves failure context. Tape validation judges capture/replay mechanics, not hash semantics; there is no independent product-result model here.

The main comparisons verify that captureHashSession reproduces the same module initialization and encounter order, including generated permutations, and rejects incomplete/excessive tapes. expectSessionLaws supplies fixed hash sanity examples across a few tapes; it does not make this replay-harness calibration an independent product owner.

The allocation counter observes production work, but the tests judge fixed constructions with literal expectations: a depth-200 shared DAG must read 400 getters, one repeated Map pair must copy entries twice, and a table supplies hand-written maximum sizes for seven shapes. The two-attempt retry examples and single opaque-handle mutation example do not provide a reusable expected-work model. Conservatively restore the original name.

Plain Map/loop/full-sort evaluators compute whole relations for consolidate, reduce, joins, grouped aggregates, and top-K. Generated input-world histories are sent through real D2 operators and judged by the companion incrementalization checker at each logical batch, including compatible split delivery.

Owns the reusable weighted-relation model, signed integration and difference, legal partition grammar, and unary/binary refinement checks. The checks compare real emitted deltas and cumulative output with independently supplied full-recomputation results and compare atomic versus split delivery. This owns judgment as well as driver mechanics.

expectedIndex independently folds each history prefix into nested native Maps using a declared type-and-value identity and signed multiplicities. After every real Index.addValue, the checker compares complete observed multiplicities and has() with that prefix model.

expectedConsolidation independently classifies the supported identity domain, groups records by direct primitive/reference or canonical structural equality, sums multiplicities, and retains the first record. Generated real MultiSet.consolidate output is checked for each exact group, weight, retained reference, omissions, duplicates, and unchanged inputs.

Despite many fixed examples later in the file, the generated sections maintain independent source Maps, recompute full ordered windows with sort/slice, and compare them with the cumulative signed TopKRelation after every real graph turn. The grammar includes replacements, transient cancellation, outer joins, and multiple production top-K variants.

The file supplies hand-written inputs and expected output arrays for initial windows and individual row changes. Its one TopKMessageTracker/TopKRelation use checks a fixed remove-b example against the literal rows a,c,d; the local helpers only sort observations. It contains no independent window recomputation or generalized history law of its own. Importing the shared checker is the borderline point; conservatively restore this filename.

Parameterized value-pair constructors define equivalence relations independently of hashing, then generated payloads and delivery order cross those relations with collision and grouping modes. The cancellation rule judges real topKBatch output, and a real ordered D2 graph must retain exactly the equivalent old row or distinct replacement with unit weight.

Only constructs TopKRelation checker instances and feeds them valid or deliberately corrupted observations to calibrate duplicate weight, retraction, index, payload, capture, and replay behavior. No real top-K production operator is exercised. The existing pre-PR oracle filename is outside the rename correction.

TopKRelation owns independent cumulative signed integration keyed by full modeled row/index identity. Its checker rejects nonunit residue, compares complete rows, derives numeric indexes from offset and position, or checks strict fractional-index order. This is reusable semantic judgment used by generated production owners; TopKMessageTracker additionally supplies capture.

An independent native Map counts typed-key support. At each generated input or window-move checkpoint, a fixed independent key order is filtered by positive support and sliced by offset/limit, then compared with the accumulated real fractional-index output and reported window size. Ordinary top-K also checks preserved multiplicity against its running input count.

expectedGroupCounts independently counts fixture-declared identity classes, and observedGroupCounts executes real D2 groupBy and records group cardinalities, unit weights, and distinct output keys. The bounded Temporal-kind cross product is judged by that class-counting rule rather than output arrays calculated separately per kind. Its oracle is narrow and based on fixed equivalence-class assignments.

expectAdmissionHistory only maps rows to value and compares them to a caller-supplied expected string array. This is a generic equality wrapper, not an independent admission state model or reference rule.

Only registers imported predicate/pagination/join/deduplication/collation/mutation/live-update suites according to capability flags. It computes no expected result and performs no independent comparison.

assertRuntimeRestartHistory encapsulates one fixed two-row write/restart/write example with literal rows and literal expected snapshots. The other exported suite cases are one fixed round-trip and fixed missing-collection error assertions. Sharing this scenario across hosts does not add an independent reference model or generalized checker.

Three hardcoded shared examples: write one fixed todo and query it, persist one fixed Collection insert and inspect its key/title through a second adapter, and assert coordinator identity. Factory injection supplies host coverage but no independently computed domain-wide result.
Four-line re-export only; it neither owns nor executes independent judgment. The model and registered property are in sqlite-core-adapter-oracle.test.ts.

Reusable host suite is a set of fixed SQL examples with literal expected rows/orders: [1,2,3] for one held transaction, [3] after one rollback, [1,3] after one nested savepoint rollback. expectAdmissionHistory receives those literal arrays; it does not derive admission from an independent schedule model.

Ordinary positive and negative TypeScript examples for one concrete RowInput/RowOutput schema, string keys, and own-key sync overloads. No generalized independent type relation or type-level algebra. Existing pre-PR oracle filename must remain unchanged despite this classification.

Mixed large file contains a genuine independent append-only durability reference: foldDurabilityLedger interprets begin/write/abort/commit events into committedRows and commitOrder without production queues. Real persisted-wrapper histories are checked against that fold at durable receipt and reopen observations; this specific mechanism, not the many fixed regressions, warrants the name.

expectedPersistedSnapshot independently computes opt-in availability, error precedence, and all-source readiness from source outcomes. A finite cross-product drives real Collections/live-query observer and compares persistedStatus, isPersistedReady, and exact error to that computation. Existing pre-PR name remains unchanged.

observeRestartOrder runs one fixed two-start cleanup/restart schedule and records counts. The generated variant only selects scheduled versus unscheduled and an incidental schemaVersion; assertions choose the fixed 1/2/4 counts for those same two schedules. No independent lifecycle model or scalable/generalized schedule judgment is present. Borderline because it uses fc.asyncProperty, but restore the original filename conservatively.

Runs assertRuntimeRestartHistory against an in-memory fake and deliberately changes score/id/extra-row/drop-next-write to ensure the checker throws. It tests checker sensitivity, not production persistence.

Contains a generalized partial admission/cardinality law: generated hydrateQueries and peerQueries control real adapter work; while the hydrate is held, admission count must not advance, and after release metadata query count must equal independently computed hydrateQueries + peerQueries. It judges variable-size production histories without consulting the scheduler; fixed cases elsewhere are not the basis for retention.

Contains generated reset/resume lineage oracle: expectedResetResumeMetadata derives exact retained metadata keys and resume kind from the declared destructive/non-destructive transition and arbitrary metadata set. observeResetResumeHistory drives real SQLite adapter transitions, then expectResetResumeLaw compares observed metadata with the independent result. The property generates rows, metadata, versions, and reopen counts.
Feeds fixed good and deliberately interleaved/missing/extra arrays to expectAdmissionHistory and asserts acceptance or throw. No production driver is used; this is checker calibration.

Mixed file contains startup reference recomputation across generated baseline sizes and managed/no-write/raw-loss transitions. Expected public rows are independently built from original baseline plus managed insert, or empty for raw loss, then compared with real Collection and durable snapshot observations. It runs the same computation in fixed and random campaigns.

Generated set/delete/clear histories update both production SortedMap and a native Map. expectMap derives expected ordering by a fresh full sort and compares every public iterator, size, membership, and value observation, including deferred-order checkpoints and three ordering modes.

Two concrete schema-transform fixtures assert RowInput/RowOutput and individual callback/parameter types with expectTypeOf and @ts-expect-error. The ItemOf extractor is ordinary type plumbing; there is no generalized independent type algebra that computes expected adapter types. Restore the PR-added oracle name.

A native Map step model independently computes operation returns and preserves both payload references and original values. Generated BTree histories are compared after each action for point reads, size/extrema, sorted full/range scans, bounds, and neighboring pairs using filtering over independently sorted model keys.

An independent keyed Map reducer applyModelOp/expectedRowsAfter computes each legal operation prefix; expectedEventTrace derives causal insert/update/delete payloads. runHistory compares actual Collection rows, callback replicas, and index observations against those computations.

stepModel independently reduces schedule/cancel/elapsed-time actions into appointments, due deliveries and errors. runHistory drives the production CleanupQueue and compares delivery/error traces after each step; generated action histories execute that rule.

expectedCleanupBoundary is an independent three-cut function of prior Collection status and cleanup boundary. Real cleanup/restart tests compare restart admission, public status, dependent termination, and settlement observations with its calculated boundary state; the file also contains ordinary regressions.

One fixed fake-timer history sets gcTime to 1, steps the wall clock backward, advances elapsed time by 10, and asserts subscriber count 1 then 0. It contains no appointment reference computation or reusable independent judgment.

One fixed idle-scheduler regression executes a no-time callback, returns/removes a subscriber, executes the rescheduled callback, and checks literal ready status. The pending callback Map is a controllable scheduler fixture, not an expected lifecycle model.

applyRound maintains independent row and metadata Maps, applying committed metadata writes to a separately cloned expected world. It derives expected change messages and callback-time metadata/row cuts and compares those with the real Collection across generated rounds.

The rejectionCases table supplies concrete mutations and per-example error assertions; subsequent startup cases assert fixed starts, handler calls, rows, and errors. The stated five admission cells are descriptive categories, not a reusable executable admission model. Existing pre-PR oracle filename is outside rename correction.

applyAction updates an independent retained-row Map from the input history, and expectRetainedState compares exposed authoritative base, public rows, and stale row-origin keys after production sync/lifecycle actions. Other sections execute the shared optimistic-history model.

Owns the independent LifecycleModel, reduceLifecycle command reducer, expected observations/trace, and deferral grammar. The history and publication owners import this model and compare real Collection observations with its transitions.

runHistory executes real subscription/lifecycle commands and separately reduces the shared LifecycleModel. assertState compares loads, unloads, caller outcomes, errors, Collection/subscription statuses, signals, and full event trace with model-derived values at every command.

The mixed file contains runAsyncRestartScenario: its independent settlement ledger derives current-generation completeness, success, retained versus replacement row version, failed attempts, publication trace, and status transitions from scenario outcomes. It compares these computed values after each controlled production settlement; this qualifies independently of its many fixed boundary examples.

Owns an independent publication model with source, visible, and private replacement Maps. publicationDiff/publishIfChanged/finishReplacement/projectPublication compute expected rows and message batches from lifecycle and source commands; the production driver compares public observations after each command.

The callback-phase × release/unsubscribe matrix runs one fixed snapshot pattern and checks literal false/no publication/one acquisition outcomes, with small phase-dependent hook/read counts. Remaining cases are pinned regressions. No independent ownership/history reducer or generalized expected-result computation is executed here. Existing pre-PR oracle filename remains unchanged.

runReplayScenario tracks independent source and published-row Maps plus pending replay state. It derives retained versus replacement publications from controlled settlement/release/source histories and compares source state, visible rows, message diffs, status, and publication counts against real subscription behavior.

runListenerScenario builds an independent ordered list of committed keys from generated commit/abort actions. It compares actual application order and batches against that list, checks aborted receipt counts/outcomes and no nested delivery, and executes exhaustive and generated histories.

The generator varies a key, two payload values, and rollback/rejection in one fixed two-owner/truncate schedule. expectObservation merely substitutes the accepted input row into a literal ready/key-set expectation; it does not reduce owner histories or compare a broader independent relation. Conservative classification as a parameterized regression; existing pre-PR name remains unchanged.

Generalized comparator laws independently constrain production ascComparator over generated values: reflexivity, antisymmetry, transitivity, and deterministic valid numeric signs. Additional value-specific comparisons use direct primitive/byte relations. Replay-calibration sections do not replace these executed product laws.

Builds synthetic disabled-result objects, mutates their fields, and verifies expectDisabledResult accepts/rejects them. It calibrates a shared assertion helper without observing production hook behavior.

Intercepts Vitest registration, injects deliberately faulty/coalesced fake drivers into the shared suite, and checks whether its concurrent-fetch scenario passes/rejects and cleans up. The object under test is the conformance runner.

Checks the test-only makeInfiniteOnDemandSource provider against literal supported/invalid requests and verifies request capture. Its additional production-query integration uses fixed expected row windows; no independent generalized product oracle is defined here.
Feeds synthetic page partitions and corrupted page arrays into expectPageRows. The randomized property generates checker inputs, rather than observing production pagination.
Tests duplicate scenario registration and failure-waiver rejection in the test registry using literal names. No production product observation.

Calibrates result-surface/equality helpers with synthetic rows, generated duplicate groups, wrong order, and wrong keyed values. Generated samples remain inputs to the checker under test, not product observations.
Exercises the ScenarioLifetime test resource manager with successful/failed cleanups, aggregate errors, and late acquisitions. These are harness lifecycle checks rather than product laws.

Checks ScenarioSources/ScenarioLifetime ownership, source cleanup, duplicate handles, and error aggregation. Although one case allocates a real Collection, the judged contract is test-harness disposal.
Checks the test scope-setup wrapper preserves successful values and combines setup/disposal failures. No production query/reference comparison.
Type/interface declarations for source handles, operation access, result surfaces, and LiveQueryDriver. They describe adapter plumbing and contain no executable independent judgment.

Reusable fixed assertion template requires disabled status/flags and either absent values or empty reactive containers. It does not compute a modeled result or a generalized relation beyond those two literal shapes; conservatively restore the helper name.
Interfaces describe infinite-query config, result, handles, and driver operations; the file contains no executable window reference computation.

Controlled test provider copies request inputs, filters/sorts a finite backend, and writes resulting rows into production sync. Its evaluator generates provider input responses; it never judges expected versus observed production output. The shared infinite suite owns that judgment.

expectedOverlappingWindow independently derives visible rows, page slices/params, continuation, fetching, error, and status from modeled source extent and settlement flags. The overlapping preload/fetch scenario enumerates source sizes and settlement orders, applies source changes, and compares the real exported controller snapshot to this model.

expectPageRows independently computes complete page count and page slices from expected rows/pageSize, and enforces reconstruction of data by flattening pages. The shared infinite suite applies this generalized page-partition law to real hook observations.

Generic selected-row normalization and ordered/unordered/keyed equality helpers compare actual data with caller-supplied expected data. They do not derive domain expected results; the infinite suite and page checker own their independent window/partition computations.

Registers reusable fixed conformance examples over SEED and hand-authored mutations. basic-select expects a literal John Smith row; equality-filter transitions expect literal ID arrays and final rows. Reuse across framework drivers and generic equality helpers does not provide an independent query evaluator or state model.

Independent scalar and tuple comparison functions define continuation and ordering. The checker evaluates the expression returned by real buildCursor with a reference evaluator and compares its denotation to the direct boundary rule; public Collection ordered snapshots after preload are compared with independently derived tuple order.

Source operations update an independent source-row Map. Signed production reconciliation outputs are integrated into a separate weighted relation and compared with one unit contribution per expected source row; the production reconciler is the system under test, not the source of expected values.
referenceRows independently folds initial rows and declarative adapter/hydration history; runHistory compares synced data, public rows, and a subscription mirror against that recomputation.

Concrete DbClient dependency, descriptor, hydration payload, preload, and schema type assertions. Expected types are explicitly written for the examples; there is no independent generalized type relation.

Fixed client isolation, hydration, serialization, and cleanup regressions, including parameterized insert/delete authority cases. No reusable independent state/reference computation judges these observations; the separate hydration-authority oracle owns that model.

A fixed matrix crosses two reentry sites, handler pending/synchronous, and three outcomes for the same three-caller disposal schedule. Assertions check literal one-release/no-early-settlement outcomes and equality of the three returned results. There is a useful common-result relation, but no separate reusable disposal/history checker; conservatively retain example classification. Existing pre-PR name remains unchanged.

expectedChanges executes operations on independent plain copies and derives changed/deleted fields. runHistory compares both production tracking paths with that result, including a separate modeled error outcome, across generated histories.

expectedSuggestions computes the policy from advice-enabled, Collection size, indexing mode and indexed field. A finite scenario domain drives real query/index suggestion creation, and the result is compared to the computed expected count. This is a small independent decision rule, not merely per-scenario expected literals. Existing pre-PR name stays untouched.

A native Map owns the expected key/value rows through generated put, delete, and rebuild histories. Fresh grouping, sorting, and direct range predicates derive expected lookups and complete memberships for both real index types; the same independent model also checks a separately rebuilt index.

Independent listener-eligibility and delivery state machine: subscribeModel, publishModel, and disposeModel evolve expected state; runHistory drives the real observer and compares exact delivery history, source state, and snapshots after commands.

Focused observer regressions assert concrete snapshot, publication, listener, and lifecycle outcomes. Setup helpers construct sources; no independent history model is executed in this file. The independent eligibility model is in the separate observer-history file.

Mixed file, but observe runs the same write history through two distinct paths: direct local-only writes and the explicitly confirmed optimistic path. The test compares their computed rows, batches, errors and transaction states. The differential mechanism at 263–266 qualifies independently of surrounding hardcoded guard regressions.

Concrete default/explicit/schema-inferred, branded and numeric key fixtures assert callback types and rejected assignments. IsAny is a helper for an ordinary type assertion, not an independent type model/algebra. Classify as examples under the corrected rule, while leaving the existing pre-PR oracle filename untouched.

Generated source histories drive a real Collection and live-query Collection. The shared independent expectNotificationHistory checker reconstructs membership and previous values from callback messages and checks callback snapshots against input-derived expected worlds; post-unsubscribe silence is also checked.

A fixed cleanup/restart scenario is repeated across observer mode and resumption variants, then asserts literal empty data and Map results. No independent state machine or differential result computation.

Although much of this file is fixed regression coverage, its permutation tests execute an independent snapshot ledger: expected snapshots are assembled from input patches, active owners select the newest surviving snapshot, and a reducer excludes rolled-back owners. Real source rows, event replicas, and downstream rows are compared with the computed snapshot.

Defines the reusable independent HistoryModel over base rows, ordered intents and source batches, plus generic event/outcome comparisons. runOptimisticHistory drives a real Collection and compares reads, event replicas and downstream rows to model state after each action. This module has no test registration; its importing test owners execute it.

The product-test section builds failed-write/peer-survival histories from generated scenarios and executes runOptimisticHistory, which computes expected rows, callbacks and promise outcomes independently. The file also contains harness calibration tests, but is not solely a harness test.

Pinned source/optimistic histories execute the shared independent HistoryModel/refinement check via runOptimisticHistory; this file supplies action sequences rather than hardcoded expected rows or batches. It also runs deliberate captured-observation corruptions through the same checker. Retained because the production outcome is judged by the reusable model, not by the example names.

Boundary case corpus invokes runOptimisticHistory for every initial-state/action program. Although the corpus is fixed and looks like a regression table, it supplies no expected-result literals: the independent shared model computes and compares every public cut. This qualifies as execution of a reusable oracle under the supplied rule, not only hardcoded regression assertions.

runSameKey independently reduces operation sequences into net mutation payloads and outcomes, while runTransaction computes proposed public rows in plain Maps and checks source/read/replica/downstream observations. Generated payloads and operation-order matrices execute those computations. Ordinary replacement examples elsewhere do not determine the classification.

Exercises guarded replay subprocess selection, execution counts, property/reporting failures, cleanup diagnostics, and manifest mapping. These assertions judge oracle execution/reporting infrastructure rather than a production data or lifecycle law. Its existing filename is outside rename correction.

queueStarts/debounceStarts/throttleStarts/nonLeadingThrottleStarts simulate starts from action histories with an independent virtual clock and ordered call IDs. Scenario expectations call these models; runProduction observations of real paced mutations are compared to the computed starts and transaction grouping.

Mixed contract/example file contains actual native differential judgment: reorder executes on an independent native Map/Set row and on the draft/Collection production paths, then compares detached and stored iteration contents to the native result across container and operation alternatives. This mechanism, not the surrounding contract prose or fixed expected assertions, warrants the name.

Native differential iteration rule executes the same iterator/edit program on a native array and a production draft, computing expected visits/final contents. A separate Map/Set run computes native membership-change observations and compares the production draft and extracted changes across iteration protocols.

expectArrayCall and expectTypedCall execute the same built-in method on separate native and draft values; native outcomes, identity and post-write values supply the independent expected result. Arbitraries vary rows, method and arguments and feed that differential checker.

Mostly unit examples, but it actually contains a reusable native array callback oracle: observeArrayCallbacks executes each history step on independent native/proxy rows, derives the expected change set from the native row, and assertArrayCallbacks compares every recorded cut. Generated two-step callbacks invoke this mechanism, so the mixed file qualifies.

Independent plain-data Spec state reducer step plus canonical equality computes expected changes after generated histories. expectHistory drives createChangeProxy and checks changed keys/values, final draft and untouched baseline against that model.

AggregateRow fixtures and concrete expectTypeOf assertions specify numeric/orderable result types and rejected inputs. Generic forwarders exercise production overloads before concrete assertions; they do not implement a generalized independent aggregate type algebra.
Unit examples for proxy paths, descriptors, identity, type guards, and literal wrapping. Expected paths/descriptors/values are literal examples, with no independent reusable semantic model.

Maintains independent source rows and recomputes the cold join with plain nested filtering/mapping. The checker compares both live output and subscription replica to those rows, and requires a real cold acquisition.

Mixed unit file contains an independent dynamic-programming LIKE/ILIKE interpreter (referenceLike), generated string/pattern cases, and findLikeMismatch comparisons against compiled production expressions.

Three lexical-source targeting examples: matching fallback alias, mismatched fallback alias, and dotted versus nested paths. Each checks a hardcoded target/path result; no independent resolver or generated law checker.

runFlushHistory tracks an independent expected row Map through generated insert/update histories, drives real derived reconciliation beneath deletes, and compares published rows and a lookup-work bound after removing the overlay.

Computes expected complete output bags using plain row mapping/nested-loop joins for each query shape and alias assignment; compares both executions to independent output and checks explicit-shape equivalence. Also owns an explicit equality-partition checker.

recompute() independently filters and orders source-Map children per parent. collectionProjection compares real live-query rows, callback publications and diff-derived parent events against that recomputation across generated CollectionAction histories; this is more than the neighboring fixed facade examples.

Recursive-source cells keep modelRows and compute expected filter/projection/aggregate/having/ordered-window results in JavaScript, then compare all public materialization forms against expected(parent.id) after real source updates. The finite grammar executes an independent result rule, alongside fixed path examples.
